result.topic_en: Ramanujan evaluates an infinite-product integral, involving the factors $1+(x/(a+2k-1))^2$ and $1+(x/(b+2k-1))^2$ times $1/(1+n^2x^2)$, as a gamma-function quotient times a continued fraction, and states that for $n=1$ the continued fraction equals an alternating series.
result.transcription:
$\int_0^\infty \frac{1}{\{1+(\frac{x}{a+1})^2\}\{1+(\frac{x}{a+3})^2\}\{1+(\frac{x}{a+5})^2\}\cdots\cdots} \cdot \frac{1}{\{1+(\frac{x}{b+1})^2\}\{1+(\frac{x}{b+3})^2\}\{1+(\frac{x}{b+5})^2\}\cdots} \cdot \frac{dx}{1+n^2x^2}$
$= 2\sqrt{\pi}\cdot\frac{\Gamma(1+\frac{a}{2})\Gamma(1+\frac{b}{2})\Gamma(1+\frac{a+b}{2})}{\Gamma(\frac{1+a}{2})\Gamma(\frac{1+b}{2})\Gamma(\frac{1+a+b}{2})}\cdot\cfrac{1}{a+b+1+\cfrac{1(a+1)(b+1)(a+b+1)n^2}{a+b+3+\cfrac{2(a+2)(b+2)(a+b+2)n^2}{a+b+5+\cdots\cdots}}}$
$a+1$ and $b+1$ being positive.
If $n=1$, the continued fraction can be shown to be equal to the series
$\frac{1}{a+b+1}\left(1 - A_1 + A_1A_2 - A_1A_2A_3 + \cdots\right)$
where $A_t = \frac{(a+t)(b+t) [-- ab\cos^2\frac{\pi t}{2}-]}{(a+1+t)(b+1+t) [-- ab\cos^2\frac{\pi t}{2}-]}$
